name: new_zeros
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::new_zeros(Tensor self, SymInt[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, mutation and alias contract, and these tests must never be removed or narrowed to fit this single signature. Other registered ATen signatures supplied for this operator: aten::new_zeros.out(Tensor self, SymInt[] size, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics derived from the tests: new_zeros is a factory that allocates a fresh, zero-filled tensor of the requested size; it ignores the source tensor's shape and strided/offset/expanded geometry, and with no keyword override the output inherits the source dtype and device. The dtype, layout, device and pin_memory keywords override the corresponding output metadata. The returned tensor is a brand-new buffer, never an alias of the source storage, the source tensor (and its whole parent storage) is left unmodified, and the result is not differentiable (requires_grad is False and grad_fn is None) even when the source tracks gradients. The pytest suite additionally exercises the .out overload (zeroing and returning the supplied buffer in place, resizing it when needed, and preserving a strided output view's storage and storage offset), dense and sparse (COO/CSR/CSC) layouts, explicit device and pinned host output, and negative cases: non-integer or non-sequence extent arguments raise TypeError or RuntimeError, negative extents raise RuntimeError, invalid dtype values raise TypeError or RuntimeError, and block-sparse or 1-D compressed-sparse requests raise RuntimeError. Effect and alias behavior differ per overload (the .out overload mutates its out parameter and returns an alias of it); such conditional behavior is not expressed by this representative-only model and remains owned by the pytest. Defaults rendered as JSON null correspond to the ATen None defaults.
